Distraction by the neighbour’s dog, intricate movements with the mower, reaching down from a moving mower, the fall and dislocation, and the mower’s automatic drive continuing onto and through the pool cover are negligent operation of employer equipment in the performance of the very task he was hired to do. That is a negligent mode of performance within the general field of activity assigned by Evergreen.

Evergreen is vicariously liable and Mark is personally liable. Evergreen and Mark are jointly and severally liable for the pool cover replacement, removal and clean-up costs. The neighbour’s short fence and the dog are background to Mark’s distraction only; they do not make the neighbours concurrent tortfeasors and do not break the close connection to the employment.

Lincoln – Ferrari scratches
Lincoln was on site in working hours with employer-supplied rake and blower raking leaves on the area he was contracted to maintain. The pleaded fact is decisive: he “went over the area with the blower as he normally would” on lawn immediately adjacent to Bruce’s parked Ferrari and the force of the blower propelled small rocks into the car causing barely noticeable scratches.

Use of the employer blower on the assigned lawn area at the client site during working hours is a mode of carrying out the leaf-clearing work. The risk that blowing debris will move loose material onto adjacent property, including a vehicle on the adjoining driveway, is a foreseeable incident of that work.

Personal dislike for Bruce, admiration of the car and Bruce’s absence go to motive only. Motive does not by itself sever a sufficiently close connection. There is no pleading that Lincoln abandoned his duties, left the work site, or used the blower for a purpose unrelated to leaf clearing. The means of commission – employer equipment, employer assignment, client property, working hours – remain within the field of activity. This is negligent performance of the employment task, not a frolic or intentional wrong done for a purely personal purpose outside the employment.

De minimis quantum affects damages only, not the existence of duty, breach or vicarious liability.

Evergreen is therefore vicariously liable for Lincoln’s negligent blower use and Lincoln is personally liable. Evergreen and Lincoln are jointly and severally liable for the Ferrari scratch loss, distinct and separate from the Evergreen and Mark liability for the pool loss.

No liability attaches to Bruce’s neighbours, Mark and Lincoln are not jointly and severally liable for each other’s independent acts, and minimal damage does not eliminate liability. That is the attribution in E: Evergreen and Mark jointly and severally for Mark’s actions; Evergreen and Lincoln jointly and severally for Lincoln’s actions.

8.text:
E

The Ontario respondeat superior test is a sufficiently close connection between the wrongful act and the general field of activity for which the employee is engaged. The employer is vicariously liable for a tort committed in the course of employment and the employee remains personally liable, so the employer and the tortfeasor employee are jointly and severally liable for the loss caused by that employee. Liability tracks each employee separately.

Mark – pool/cover/mower loss
Mark was on Bruce’s property on 1 Oct 2021 during working hours operating Evergreen’s riding lawnmower to cut grass, the work he was hired to do. Distraction by the neighbour’s dog, intricate movements, reaching down from a moving mower, the fall/dislocation and the mower’s automatic drive continuing onto and through the pool cover is negligent operation of employer equipment in the performance of the very field of activity assigned by Evergreen. It is a negligent mode of performance closely connected to Evergreen’s business, on the work site with employer supplied equipment at working hours.

Evergreen is vicariously liable and Mark is personally liable. Evergreen and Mark are jointly and severally liable for the pool cover replacement, mower removal and pool clean-up. The neighbours’ short fence and the dog are background to the distraction only; they do not create a duty/breach by the neighbours and do not sever the close connection.

Lincoln – Ferrari scratches
Lincoln was on site in working hours with employer supplied rake and blower raking/blowing leaves on the area he was contracted to maintain. The pleaded fact is decisive: he “went over the area with the blower as he normally would” on lawn immediately adjacent to Bruce’s parked Ferrari and the blower force propelled small rocks causing barely noticeable scratches.

Using the employer blower on the assigned lawn area at the client property during working hours is the employment task itself. The risk that blowing work will move debris and loose rocks onto adjacent property, including a vehicle on the driveway, is a foreseeable incident inherent in residential leaf-clearing work.

Personal dislike for Bruce, admiring the car and Bruce’s absence go to motive only. There is no pleading of abandonment of duties, a personal errand, or use of the blower for a purpose unrelated to leaf clearing. The means of commission remain employer blower, employer assignment, client property, working hours – i.e. within the field of activity. That is negligent performance of the authorized task, not a frolic or an intentional wrong done for purely personal reasons outside the scope.

De minimis quantum affects damages only, not duty, breach or vicarious liability. Evergreen is vicariously liable for Lincoln’s negligent blower use and Lincoln is personally liable.

Liability therefore tracks separately: Evergreen and Mark are jointly and severally liable for the damage resulting from Mark’s actions; Evergreen and Lincoln are jointly and severally liable for the damage resulting from Lincoln’s actions. Mark and Lincoln are not jointly and severally liable for each other’s independent torts and Bruce’s neighbours are not liable.

reflection_text.9:
The discussion remains unanimous on E in round 4; all 12 colleagues now explicitly endorse E. Colleagues 6 and 9 who held minority C in round 0 have fully abandoned the frolic/intentional-motive argument for Lincoln and now endorse E.

Current consensus attribution:
* Mark / pool loss: Evergreen Grass Care Ltd and Mark are jointly and severally liable for damage resulting from Mark’s actions. Evergreen is vicariously liable under respondeat superior for a negligent tort committed in the course of employment; Mark is personally liable. The negligence is the negligent mode of performance of cutting grass with employer riding mower on client property during working hours – distraction, intricate movements, reaching down from moving mower, fall, automatic-drive mower continuing into pool. Close connection / field of activity satisfied. Neighbours’ short fence / dog are background distraction only, no duty/breach/causation, no joint liability.
* Lincoln / Ferrari scratch loss: Evergreen Grass Care Ltd and Lincoln are jointly and severally liable for damage resulting from Lincoln’s actions. Evergreen is vicariously liable for negligent blower use in the course of employment; Lincoln is personally liable. Work site, working hours, employer-supplied rake/blower, assignment to rake/blow leaves on lawn immediately adjacent to Ferrari. Pleading decisive: “went over the area with the blower as he normally would”. Risk that blowing will propel rocks/debris onto adjacent property/vehicle is foreseeable inherent incident of residential leaf-clearing. Motive – Lincoln despises Bruce, admires car, Bruce absent – goes to motive only; no abandonment of duties, no personal errand, no use of blower for purpose unrelated to leaf clearing. No frolic; negligent performance of authorised task, not intentional wrong for purely personal reasons. De minimis quantum affects damages only, not duty/breach/vicarious liability.

Key legal points retained across rounds:
* Ontario respondeat superior: employer vicariously liable for tort in course of employment; employee remains personally liable → employer + employee jointly and severally for that employee’s loss. Liability tracks separately per employee; no cross joint-and-several liability between Mark and Lincoln.
* Close connection test satisfied for both via employer equipment, employer assignment, client property, working hours, negligent mode of performance.
* Motive does not sever connection absent abandonment/frolic.
* De minimis is quantum.
* Neighbours not liable.

Changes from earlier rounds:
* Round 0 minority C view from Colleagues 6 and 9 – arguing Lincoln’s animus + absence made blower use an intentional personal frolic outside scope, so only Lincoln personally liable – has been abandoned. Both now accept motive irrelevant without abandonment and act is negligent work performance.
* Options rejected unanimously: A neighbours jointly and severally liable for Mark’s damage / only Lincoln liable for his own; B Evergreen, Mark and Lincoln jointly and severally for all damage; C Evergreen+Mark for Mark; only Lincoln for Lincoln; D no liability for Lincoln because minimal damage.

Unresolved residual nuance remains conceptual: analysis would change if facts showed affirmative intentional targeting for personal spite rather than negligent leaf clearing. On present wording “as he normally would” consensus is negligent performance within scope.

Current belief: E is correct. Evergreen and Mark jointly and severally for Mark’s actions; Evergreen and Lincoln jointly and severally for Lincoln’s actions.
